title: Edmund and the Monsoon
premise: August Ravensworth, a disgraced mountain guide drowning in debt to a smuggler named Corvo, is hired by a mining consortium to find the Halcyon Expedition, which went silent while surveying a river valley in monsoon country. What he finds is a survivor, Dr. Ilsa Vane, guarding a discovery the consortium will kill to control: a vein of rare earth ore beneath a living village. As the monsoon breaks and Corvo's men close in, August must choose between paying his debt with blood or burning his last chance at redemption. He leads the villagers and Ilsa out through flooded gorges, destroys the survey data, and turns himself in—buying the valley's silence with his own freedom.
about_author: Juniper Montrose is a former river outfitter who spent a decade leading expeditions across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who carry their mistakes into wild places.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Compass
chapters.summary: POV August. In a border-town bar, August drinks away the last of his money while Corvo's collector reminds him of what he owes. A consortium fixer offers him a job: locate the silent Halcyon Expedition upriver. Broke and blacklisted everywhere else, he accepts. Emotional beat: a man at the bottom taking the only rope offered, not seeing it's also a noose.

chapters.title: Upstream of Silence
chapters.summary: POV August. August travels upriver with a consortium liaison, Mercer, whose polished manners hide menace. Villages along the route are empty or wary; someone paid them to forget the expedition passed. They find the expedition's abandoned second camp, ransacked but not looted. Emotional beat: creeping dread as August realizes this isn't a rescue—it's a cleanup.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: POV August. Following a torn map fragment, August finds the expedition's lead geologist dead in the shallows, notebook waterproofed against his chest. The notes describe an ore body 'beneath the village that must not be surveyed.' First contact with hostile men in the treeline; August escapes into the jungle. Emotional beat: the hunt begins, and August understands he was never meant to come back.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane, the expedition's surviving scientist, hiding with the valley villagers who sheltered her after her colleagues tried to sell the find. She distrusts August on sight, assuming he's consortium. A night raid by Mercer's scouts forces them together; she sees him take a bullet graze protecting a child. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Village Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the village, August learns the ore runs directly beneath homes and graves—the consortium's maps mean eviction or worse. Ilsa reveals the rest of the expedition died arguing over whether to report it. Corvo's name surfaces: he's financing Mercer's operation, meaning August's debt bought his passage here deliberately. Emotional beat: belonging offered exactly where survival demands betrayal.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: POV August. Mercer offers August full debt forgiveness and a clean passport if he delivers Ilsa and the survey cores. That night, Corvo himself arrives by boat, reminding August that debts don't expire—they transfer. August stalls, agreeing to think until the monsoon's first storm hits. Emotional beat: temptation laid out plainly, and the old hunger for a clean slate nearly winning.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The monsoon arrives in earnest; the river swallows the lower camps and cuts the valley's exit routes. Ilsa and August plan an escape through the flooded gorge system with eleven villagers, using the expedition's abandoned raft gear. Mercer's men seize the village headman as leverage. Emotional beat: grief for the drowned landscape becoming resolve—the price of survival is finally counted in other people.

chapters.title: The Gorge Run
chapters.summary: POV August. The escape through white water: capsized rafts, a villager lost to the current, Mercer's boats in pursuit. August uses his blacklisted knowledge of these rivers—knowledge that ruined him—to run a channel no sane guide would attempt. They lose the pursuers but surface miles downstream, battered, one fewer than they started with. Emotional beat: his disgrace transmuted into the very skill that saves them.

chapters.title: Everything He Owes
chapters.summary: POV August. Cornered at the river mouth, August trades himself to Corvo and Mercer for the villagers' safe passage, secretly passing Ilsa the geologist's notebook to destroy. But Corvo intends to kill him anyway once the cores are recovered—and Ilsa, instead of fleeing, doubles back with the villagers and the flood-swollen river itself to break the standoff. Mercer drowns; Corvo flees empty-handed. Emotional beat: the climax where August stops buying survival and starts spending himself.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: POV August, coda. Weeks later, August sits in a regional jail, having surrendered the destroyed survey's existence to authorities who quietly bury the mine claim. Ilsa visits with word that the valley stands, its location unrecorded. His debt died with Corvo's operation; his reputation may never recover. He finds he doesn't mind. Emotional beat: resolution without reward—belonging earned not by coming home, but by choosing what home means.
